designSummary: Stratified two-stage cluster sample; survey-weighted prevalence estimates and a prevalence ratio for renters versus owners.
sampleSize: Planning values: a working carbon monoxide alarm in 45 percent of owner-occupied and 30 percent of rented homes with a fuel-burning appliance. Detecting that 15-point difference with 80 percent power at two-sided alpha 0.05 needs 163 households per group; with a design effect of 1.5 for clustering this becomes 245 per group. Renters are about a quarter of households, so about 980 completed households are needed to reach 245 renters. With 60 percent response, about 1,630 addresses are sampled. The overall prevalence will then have a 95 percent confidence interval of about 3.8 percentage points either side at a prevalence of 40 percent.
primaryAnalysis: Survey-weighted prevalence of a working carbon monoxide alarm by tenure, with design weights for selection probability and nonresponse adjustment by segment and dwelling type; prevalence ratio for privately rented versus owner-occupied homes from a weighted Poisson model with robust variance that accounts for clustering.
secondaryAnalysis: Prevalence ratio adjusted for heating type, dwelling age, household size and rural or town stratum; prevalence by heating type; agreement between reported and working alarms; the same estimates for smoke alarms.
missingData: Unit nonresponse is handled by weighting classes; households that refuse the test are reported separately, and bounds are given by treating untested alarms first as working and then as not working.
multiplicity: One primary comparison; secondary estimates are reported with confidence intervals and no significance claims.
software: R with the survey package; weights and code archived before fieldwork ends.
overfittingGuards: Planning values and design effect recorded before sampling
summary: About 1,630 addresses for 980 completed visits give 80 percent power for a 15-point tenure difference after a design effect of 1.5.
